title: Interleaved retry crediting for delta/frame-based streaming semantics
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Our streaming metering pipeline currently assumes a single linear token emission path per session. Modern streaming clients and some model outputs emit delta/patch frames, and the platform also supports midstream retries/reconnects and server-initiated aborts. In practice this creates cases where provisional credits were consumed for frames that are later superseded (retries) or duplicated (client reconnects), leading to customer-visible overbilling and incorrect quota enforcement.

Goal: Design and implement a robust, low-latency accounting approach that ensures final billed token counts match the canonical terminal output while preserving SLOs for latency-sensitive streaming flows. We must handle: interleaved partial frames, out-of-order fragments, client retries, reconnect idempotency, server aborts (with partial outputs), and midstream model switches.

Proposed approach (high level):
1) Session-scoped sequence checkpoints: every streaming frame includes a session_seq and frame_id. The ingestion layer persists a lightweight checkpoint with provisional token delta for each frame.
2) Provisional credits ledger: when a frame is emitted we create a provisional credit ledger entry (TTL-based) that increments quotas/usage counters optimistically. These provisional entries can be reversed if a later reconciliation determines they were superseded or duplicate.
3) Deterministic reconciliation on terminal event: when session ends (client FIN, server terminal token, or a canonical commit event), run reconciliation that computes canonical token attribution based on final assembled output and converts provisional entries to final credits (apply adjustments/reversals).
4) Idempotent resume semantics: resume/reconnects must carry resume_token + last_ack_seq. Ingress deduplicates frames already accounted for using session_seq and frame_id checks.
5) Lightweight compacted audit trail: keep compacted per-session deltas (not full frame payloads) sufficient to recompute final token attribution for a configurable retention window (e.g., 48h) for post-facto audits.

Trade-offs considered:
- Strong consistency (write-through finalization) would avoid provisional credits but adds latency; we prefer optimistic provisional credits + fast reconciliation to keep SLOs.
- Storing full frame payloads increases storage and privacy surface; we store only token counts, seq metadata, and checksums.
- Keeping TTL too short risks not being able to reconcile for delayed joins/retries; too long wastes resources. Default TTL 48h with per-customer override.

Open questions / design points: 
- How to treat server-initiated partial aborts: bill for emitted tokens vs bill for committed tokens? Proposed: bill for emitted tokens provisionally, but allow post-abort reconciliation to credit back tokens if the final state indicates they should not count (for example, duplicates or partial echoes).
- Interaction with rate limiter and quotas: provisional credits should decrement available quota to avoid bursts, but the reconciliation step must be able to restore quota when provisional credits are reversed. We need quota headroom for reconciliations to return credits safely.
- What constitutes terminal event for streamed tool-calls vs raw generation? Agreed to use explicit terminal markers from runtime when available; otherwise fallback to inactivity TTL + client FIN.

Implementation plan (phases):
Phase 1 (ingest and provisional ledger): add session_seq and frame_id to stream envelope, persist provisional ledger entries (no payload), expose provisional_count in console for debugging. (2 weeks)
Phase 2 (reconciliation worker): implement reconciliation job that consumes terminal events and reconciles provisional entries to final credits; integration tests + performance tests. (3 weeks)
Phase 3 (resume/idempotency): ensure resume semantics include last_ack_seq; ingress dedupe layer consults per-session checkpoint. (1.5 weeks)
Phase 4 (rollout + monitoring): feature flag rollout, canary 5% -> 25% -> 100% across tenants; add dashboards for provisional vs final deltas, reconciliation latency, reversed-credit rates. (2 weeks)

Testing and validation:
- Unit tests for ledger entry lifecycle (provisional -> final -> reversed).
- E2E harness simulating reconnects, duplicated frames, server aborts, midstream model switch. Reproduce known bug patterns collected from production incidents.
- Fuzz tester that generates out-of-order frames and ensures final token counts are deterministic.
- Synthetic load test to ensure reconciliation worker keeps up at production scale and does not introduce backlog that could block quota operations.

Rollout and mitigation strategy:
- Deploy behind feature flag and start with low-risk tenants.
- Add automated rollback on two signals: reversed-credit-rate > 0.5% or reconciliation lag > 1 minute for >1% of sessions.
- Customer support playbook prepared with steps to query session audit trail and issue manual credits if needed.

Metrics to monitor (dashboards):
- provisional_credits_created/sec
- provisional_to_final_conversion_rate (target > 99.5%)
- reversed_credit_rate (target < 0.1% after canary)
- reconciliation_latency_p50/p95/p99
- quota_deficit_events_during_reconciliation
- incidents where billed_count != canonical_count (goal: 0 post-rollout)

Links / artifacts:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/METER/Interleaved+Streaming+Crediting (draft)
- Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/6792
- Test harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/metering-tests/tree/stream-delta
- Dashboard (canary): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/streaming-metering

Expected ETA: Initial canary ready by 2025-03-07.
comments: 2025-01-16: Initial triage by Michael Chen. Agreed this is P1 due to multiple customer reports of overbilling in reconnect flows.
2025-01-22: Design review notes from Lena Ortiz: prefer keeping payload out of audit trail; add frame checksum to detect silent corruption. Action: add checksum and compacted delta retention plan.

2025-01-29: Security review (informal) by Ravi Desai: storing token counts and checksums acceptable; ensure no raw text persisted and KMS-scoped access for audit worker. Marked security_review_required=false but enforce access controls.
2025-02-05: PR created (draft). Implementation of provisional ledger prototyped. Needs test harness for reconnect scenarios. @Devon Brooks volunteered to add fuzz tests.
2025-02-12: Performance sync: provisional writes add ~3% CPU at ingress under peak in prototype. Team agreed to micro-benchmark and consider batching ledger writes.
2025-02-20: Reconciliation worker MVP completed. Beginning integration tests against canary environment. Remaining: quota rollback semantics and canary dashboards.
